The Kurdish armed movement founded by Ab: The Kurdish armed movement founded by Abdullah Ocalan in 1978. It has fought the Turkish state since 1984; its command sits in the Qandil mountains of Iraqi Kurdistan. Turkey, the United States and the European Union list it as a terrorist organisation.
A Baloch separatist armed group fighting: A Baloch separatist armed group fighting for the independence of Balochistan from Pakistan, chiefly against the Pakistani security forces and Chinese-funded projects. The United States, the United Kingdom and Pakistan list it as a terrorist organisation.
An alliance of Pakistani Islamist milita: An alliance of Pakistani Islamist militant groups fighting the state in the north-west since 2007. Since the Taliban took Kabul its leadership operates from Afghanistan. Pakistan and the United States list it as a terrorist organisation.
The armed opposition to the Taliban led: The armed opposition to the Taliban led by Ahmad Massoud, son of Ahmad Shah Massoud. Its fighters hold out in the Panjshir and neighbouring valleys; its leadership lives in exile in Tajikistan and the West.
The armed group that split from the Orom: The armed group that split from the Oromo Liberation Front in 2018 and fights the Ethiopian federal government in Oromia. The government of Ethiopia calls it a terrorist organisation.
Amhara militias that fought on the gover: Amhara militias that fought on the government's side in the Tigray war and rose against it in August 2023. They have no single command.
The party that ruled Ethiopia until 2018: The party that ruled Ethiopia until 2018 and fought the federal government in 2020-2022. Since the Pretoria agreement it runs Tigray through an interim administration; the Tigray Defence Forces are partly demobilised.
The movement for an independent Biafra i: The movement for an independent Biafra in south-eastern Nigeria, founded by Nnamdi Kanu in 2012, with an armed wing, the Eastern Security Network. Nigeria has banned it as a terrorist organisation.
United Liberation Movement for West Papu: United Liberation Movement for West Papua
An umbrella of Papuan organisations purs: An umbrella of Papuan organisations pursuing self-determination for western New Guinea through peaceful means and international diplomacy; its provisional government works from Vanuatu.
The international organisation of the Uy: The international organisation of the Uyghur diaspora, headquartered in Munich, campaigning for the rights of the Uyghurs in Xinjiang. China calls it separatist.
The Belarusian opposition in exile led b: The Belarusian opposition in exile led by Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya and her United Transitional Cabinet, working from Vilnius since the election of 2020.
The government in exile of the unrecogni: The government in exile of the unrecognised Chechen state of the 1990s. Its battalions fight for Ukraine; in 2022 Ukraine's parliament declared Ichkeria temporarily occupied by Russia.
Mejlis of the Crimean Tatar People: Mejlis of the Crimean Tatar People
The representative body of the Crimean T: The representative body of the Crimean Tatars, elected by their Qurultay. Russia banned it as extremist in 2016; it has worked from Kyiv since.
Al-Qaeda's Sahel branch, formed in 2017. It controls much of the countryside of Mali and Burkina Faso and is spreading towards the coastal states of West Africa. The United Nations and many governments list it as a terrorist organisation.
The Somali Islamist group allied to al-Q: The Somali Islamist group allied to al-Qaeda. It controls much of the countryside of southern and central Somalia, where it taxes and runs courts. The United Nations, the United States and many others list it as a terrorist organisation.
The Islamic State's branch around Lake C: The Islamic State's branch around Lake Chad, split from Boko Haram in 2016. It operates in north-eastern Nigeria and the neighbouring parts of Niger, Chad and Cameroon. The United Nations and many governments list it as a terrorist organisation.
The armed wing of the United League of A: The armed wing of the United League of Arakan, the Rakhine insurgent organisation. Since November 2023 it has been on the offensive against Myanmar's military government in Rakhine State.
The Kachin political organisation and it: The Kachin political organisation and its Kachin Independence Army, at war with Myanmar's central government since 1961. Its headquarters is Laiza on the Chinese border.
The parallel government formed by the la: The parallel government formed by the lawmakers ousted in the coup of 2021 and their allies. Its People's Defence Forces fight the junta across the country, above all in Sagaing and Magway.
The Sudanese paramilitary force of Moham: The Sudanese paramilitary force of Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, Hemedti, grown out of the Janjaweed militias of Darfur. Since April 2023 it has fought the Sudanese army for power; it is accused of mass atrocities in Darfur.
The Zaydi Houthi movement, which has hel: The Zaydi Houthi movement, which has held Sanaa and north-western Yemen since 2014. Iran backs it; since November 2023 it has attacked shipping in the Red Sea.
The Islamist group grown out of al-Qaeda: The Islamist group grown out of al-Qaeda's Syrian branch, which broke with it in 2017. Through its Salvation Government it runs Idlib in north-western Syria. The United Nations, the United States and many others list it as a terrorist organisation.
The alliance of Kurdish, Arab and Assyri: The alliance of Kurdish, Arab and Assyrian forces led by the Kurdish People's Protection Units that defeated the Islamic State in north-eastern Syria. It runs the region through the Autonomous Administration, with American backing.
The armed forces of eastern Libya under: The armed forces of eastern Libya under Khalifa Haftar, answering to the House of Representatives in Tobruk. They have stood against the government in Tripoli since 2014 and tried to take the capital in 2019-2020.
